name: Australia
headline: Australia: +2.0% growth in 2025, 2.8% inflation, debt 52% of GDP
sections: Australia is a $1.84 trillion economy (2025), the world's 15th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +2.0% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $72K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 5.3% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose 2.8% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 6.6% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 4.2% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 9.6% (2025).
Gross government debt is 52% of GDP (2025), a moderate level that has fallen from 57% in 2020. The general government balance is −2.9% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is −2.6% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 46% of GDP (2025), a relatively closed economy. Net FDI inflows were 2.1% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 54% of GDP by 2031, broadly stable from today's level. Life expectancy is 83.1 years (2024). Population: 27.7 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
